D-001.rationale: R03 has an absolute 400-participant cap and R04 guarantees a speaker ticket even at full capacity. The finding identifies the exact incompatible admission rules.

D-002.rationale: R08 requires partial or zero refunds in later periods; R09 mandates a full refund for every website-paid cancellation. This identifies both contradictory outcomes.

D-003.rationale: Same refund schedule versus full-refund integration decision as D-002; no independent corrective decision.

D-004.rationale: Same R08/R09 conflict already accepted at D-002; rephrasing and evidence selection do not create a new root.

D-005.rationale: R05 expires seat holds while R06 allows later payment confirmation; the finding correctly asks how the ticket and money are handled after release.

D-006.rationale: R11 leaves the activity-based ranking and tie resolution unspecified; these are needed for selection among applicants.

D-007.rationale: R12 requires legal name and tax ID on an invoice but specifies no input source for them; the report identifies that missing data path.

D-008.rationale: R13 does not specify an acceptable service/queue time or measurement conditions; the cited finding identifies the untestable speed requirement.

D-009.rationale: R11 expressly configures an application-review deadline but does not define what happens to pending applications when it expires. This deadline outcome is distinct from the selection ranking criterion.

D-010.rationale: R01 clearly gives compatible dates and start time for one conference schedule. Splitting these into two traceability units is an editorial preference, not a source defect or missing decision.
